value.rationale: Reusing a sampled factor is an economically motivated attempt to reduce structured-sketch sampling and setup cost. The sharp rank/probe phase boundary and nondegenerate infinite-sample limit explain precisely why repeated right-factor samples cannot compensate: moment existence stops at matrix rank even if the number of probes grows. This is a structural risk for a natural computational modification, not merely a renamed Gaussian product or a small numerical gain.
